# The fields generated by a symmetric element

Let \(f\) be monic and irreducible over a field \(E\), with irreducible coefficient extension \(p\) over an extension field \(K\). The map of root algebras takes the root of \(f\) to the root of \(p\). `symmetricRootField` is its image inside the upper root field. This puts both root fields in the universe of \(K\). Their degrees over \(E\) and \(K\), respectively, are the degree of \(f\). The tensor product of the lower field with \(K\) is the upper field. The map from the tensor product is surjective because the upper root is in its image, and the degree formulas give equal dimensions. In particular, if \(K/E\) is quadratic, the extension of the two root fields is quadratic.

For an element \(a\) of a \(K\)-algebra with \(p(a)=0\), `rootAlgebraEvaluation` maps the upper root algebra into that algebra. Evaluation on polynomials descends through the ideal generated by \(p\) and works in a possibly noncommutative target. If \(a\) is fixed by an involution linear over \(E\), the image of the lower root field is fixed because it consists of evaluations of \(E\)-polynomials in \(a\). For an irreducible reduced characteristic polynomial of a symmetric element, the descended polynomial has the required root and irreducibility properties by reduced Cayley–Hamilton and reflection of irreducibility from \(K\) to \(E\).

For a degree-\(n\) central simple algebra with CM involution and \(f\) of degree \(n\), `reducedNorm_symmetricRootField` computes the reduced norm of a lower-field element as its field norm to \(E\) followed by the center inclusion. On the embedded upper field of degree \(n\), the reduced norm is its field norm to \(K\). The tensor identification and scalar extension of determinants then give the claimed formula.
